opening.argument: Judge, the distinction between an entry and an awarded gift card matters. The page shown says “WIN $5,000” and later displays an “Official Entry Form”—language consistent with entering a promotion, not proof that every visitor receives a prize. The closing “IT WORKS 100%” is emphatic, but the footage does not establish what that claim refers to or show a gift card being delivered. Read the claim cautiously rather than treating an unverified outcome as an observed deception.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening rightly identifies a free-gift-card title and a form requesting personal details. But the form establishes an entry process, not what happens to the information afterward; the “WIN $5,000” page also frames participation as a chance to win. Even the forceful “IT WORKS 100%” card does not demonstrate that a promised gift card failed to arrive.

opening.argument: Judge, this can be read as a screen-recorded walkthrough of an online process. The sampled sequence shows a search-results page, a page spelling out “Click ‘Claim,’” “Enter Info,” and “Check Email,” and then the entry form itself. Showing those steps lets viewers inspect the process instead of concealing it. The closing request to “LIKE AND SUBSCRIBE FOR MORE HACKS” also fits a how-to-video presentation. The footage documents a route through web pages; it does not document a completed gift-card delivery or what happens to submitted details.

rebuttal.rebuttal: A walkthrough is not automatically an instruction to surrender information. The visible claim steps and form show viewers what the process asks of them, while the prosecution’s opening does not establish that the creator controls the destination or that any submitted details were misused. The description links to the offer, but a link alongside a demonstrated process does not, by itself, settle its legitimacy.

opening.argument: Judge, an online prize entry can be an ordinary promotion without being certified as safe. The shown page invites visitors to “WIN $5,000,” supplies an “ENTER HERE!” button, and proceeds to an “Official Entry Form.” Those screens explain why contact and delivery details appear: they are part of the displayed entry flow. The cited material does not show a required deposit, an investment return, account credentials, or a downstream outcome. Treating the form alone as proof of a scam would collapse the distinction between a promotion that collects entry details and proven misuse of them.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a strong pitch, but its opening concedes that no submitted-information outcome or gift-card delivery is shown. The title’s free-gift-card claim and the form’s personal-detail fields may warrant caution; they do not establish a deposit demand, credential theft, or actual misuse. “IT WORKS 100%” is promotional language, not independent evidence of what happened after entry.
